transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42m
Recording: yes
Attendees: Austen (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Head of ML), Carlos (Infra), Ella (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Customer evaluating quick time-to-first-token (TTFT) vs private deployment for a compliance-sensitive recommender/prose assistant.
- Primary constraints: SOC2+ data retention, customer-managed KMS, VPC peering requirement, and sub-150ms p95 latency targets for a light assistant use case.
- Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on Redwood Hosted with a plan to run dedicated/private latency benchmarks if hosted doesn't meet SLOs.
- Next: Redwood will send pilot plan, pricing/credit estimate, and a security packet; customer to share promptset and infra contacts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Austen: hey everyone, thanks for carving time — quick intros?
[00:04] Priya: hi Priya here, head of ML at Orchard Ridge, small team building an advisor assistant for our retail banking product. we care a lot about latency and privacy, hi.
[00:10] Carlos: Carlos, infra lead, I'll focus on connectivity and certs.
[00:13] Ella: Ella, security and compliance, i'll be looking at audit logs and kms flows.
[00:17] Austen: great. maya and jonah are with me — maya will be the SE on the account and can dig into perf details.
[00:24] Maya: hey all. excited to dig in.
[00:26] Jonah: hi, i'll help scope the pilot and the support side.
[00:29] Austen: objective for today: understand your stack, constraints, success criteria and map TTFT options — self-serve hosted credits, dedicated reserved, or our private VPC/on-prem path. sound good?
[00:37] Priya: yes. quick context: we have a regulated dataset — customer PII in prompts sometimes — so we need encryption at rest and key control. we also need to prove latency. target p95 under 150ms for short prompts, and cost per request matters since we'll scale.
[00:52] Ethan (background noise, mis-attributed): mm-hmm
[00:54] Maya: got it. on the privacy front we support hosted with SOC2, optional Bring-Your-Own-KMS for key separation, and Private (VPC) deployments where control plane is customer-managed. both options have audit logs and retention settings.
[01:08] Priya: BYOK? can we keep keys in our HSM?
[01:12] Maya: yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated setups; hosted API can also be configured to use a customer KMS on enterprise plans, or we can use envelope encryption. i'll share the security packet.
[01:22] Ella: are there attestations for access by redwood engineers in private mode? we need zero engineer ingress unless we approve.
[01:28] Jonah: in Private there's an admin plane we can hand over; engineer access is restricted and logged, and we have role-based access controls; if you need air-gapped we have an on-prem package.
[01:40] Carlos: connectivity — we need VPC peering not just an internet endpoint, and support for private link? what's supported?
[01:47] Maya: we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink; for GCP we do VPC-SC style private access. pt note: sometimes phrased as 'Redwood Privatee' in older docs — ignore that typo — but basically private connectivity is supported.
[01:59] Priya: great. now on latency: do you have bench numbers for small assistant queries? p95, p99?
[02:06] Maya: depends on model and either continuous batching or no-batching. for hosted we have low-latency paths, optimized kernels and kv-cache to speed repeated contexts. typical p95 for 1.5k token context with a 7B-ish model on hosted can be <120ms for generation-only short outputs, but that depends on batching and your exact prompt length — those public numbers are approximate.
[02:27] Priya: hmm, our prompt size is small, often 40-80 tokens and reply 60-120 — so your numbers sound promising. what's the TTFT for our team if we want to hack something in?
[02:38] Austen: quickstart: you can sign up self-serve, get credits, and call the API within minutes. typical TTFT for dev prototype is under 1 hour to first token if you follow the quickstart. for a production pilot with telemetry and canary rollout we'll usually recommend a two-week pilot so we can run representative latency tests and tweak batching/quantization profiles.
[02:55] Priya: two weeks pilot — that fits our org. we want to test hosted first and only move to dedicated/private if hosted fails to meet SLOs. is that a common path?
[03:05] Maya: yes, we see that frequently — hosted for rapid TTFT then dedicated pools or private for hard isolation. we can mirror the production traffic in the hosted pilot, and we have tooling to pin model versions and fallback to quantized variants if perf suggests.
[03:18] Carlos: about dedicated: is that reserved GPU pools? how quickly can you provision?
[03:22] Jonah: dedicated is reserved capacity — generally provisioned within days once contract/commit is in place; for urgent needs we have a burst policy for early spikes. provisioning time varies by region and sku availability.
[03:33] Priya: ok. what about cost signals? we need unit economics per 1k tokens and per request. is that in the pilot?
[03:40] Maya: yes we'll include token breakdown in the pilot dashboard. Redwood Optimize suggestions will propose batching and quantization if they help reduce cost while keeping quality.
[03:49] Ella: compliance: do you have SOC2 type II, ISO?
[03:52] Maya: SOC2 type II yes, and ISO 27001 for the enterprise offering. we'll send certs and the security whitepaper.
[03:58] Ella: what about data residency — logs in EU vs US?
[04:02] Maya: hosted allows region pinning; for strict residency we'd recommend dedicated or private where we can host within your region and honor retention policies.
[04:10] Priya: for our first pilot we want: hosted in us-west, BYOK if possible, run latency benchmarks vs our internal baseline, and share failure modes. can the pilot include tail-latency breakdowns and token-level costs?
[04:22] Austen: absolutely — our console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per route/model and we'll share access during the pilot.
[04:28] Priya: perfect. are you able to run quality parity tests against our baseline model? we might compare responses for a hand-graded set.
[04:35] Maya: yes; please send a prompt set and expected responses or eval rubrics. we can run automated evals and a human-in-the-loop check; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization only if quality thresholds pass.
[04:47] Carlos: network security again — do you support mTLS for service-to-service?
[04:51] Jonah: mTLS yes for Private and Dedicated; hosted has TLS endpoint and PrivateLink option if you need private connectivity.
[04:57] Ella: audit logs — are they immutable, how long retained, and can we export to our SIEM?
[05:03] Maya: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3/Cloud Logging and retention is configurable. immutable logs via append-only and signed entries are on our enterprise retention add-on.
[05:12] Priya: ok. timeline — we want to have a pilot kicking off next week, run two weeks, and then decision point. what do you need from us?
[05:19] Austen: a short list: 1) sample prompt set (20-50 prompts) and a small dataset slice, 2) access contact for infra VPN/peering, 3) security requirements doc — we'll send our pilot scope and an MSA addendum for pilot credits.
[05:32] Priya: i'll circulate that today.
[05:34] Carlos: about the prompt set — we also want to include high-concurrency tests to see queuing under load.
[05:39] Maya: we'll simulate concurrency and can test autoscaling on Dedicated in a follow-up if needed. for hosted, we can replay traffic patterns to approximate concurrency effects.
[05:49] Priya: excellent. any notable limitations — e.g., long conversation KV cache mismatch or prompt truncation we should be aware of?
[05:56] Maya: yes long historical contexts are truncated per model's max tokens, but we support KV cache and prefix caching to accelerate repeated contexts. there's also a subtlety with quantized model variants — rare edge cases where subtle generation artifacts can appear, so we'll run quality gating before any quantization.
[06:12] Priya: mention of 'KV cache' in docs was a bit fuzzy — can you send an explainer?
[06:16] Maya: sure, i'll include a short tech note on KV/prefix caching and how it affects latency.
[06:20] Ella: two security things: 1) we need an explicit statement about Redwood engineer access during pilot, and 2) data deletion guarantees after pilot end.
[06:29] Jonah: we can provide an engineer access policy and an on-demand deletion certificate; for hosted pilots we'll document retention and deletion flows in the security packet.
[06:36] Priya: good. pricing/credits — how many credits for a two-week hosted pilot with 100k requests simulated? ballpark.
[06:42] Austen: rough estimate: depends on model size and tokens per request; for budgeting assume 100k requests * avg 200 tokens/request at our dev rate — we'll include a clearer credit estimate in the pilot plan. we can also offer a capped credit amount for the pilot under the MSA addendum.
[06:58] Priya: do you have standard pilot MSA language?
[07:02] Jonah: yes, short pilot addendum — we'll share it. it covers limited liability, credit cap, data handling, and templates for SSO/SAML setup.
[07:10] Carlos: SSO — we use SAML with Okta, need to sync accounts for console access.
[07:14] Maya: Okta SAML is supported; we'll send SSO setup steps.
[07:18] Priya: about metrics: we want to see p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, error rates, and quality KG (like BLEU or human scores). do you calculate ROUGE/BLEU?
[07:27] Maya: we run automated metrics and can plug in custom evals; we'll surface those in the console and in the pilot deliverable.
[07:33] Ella: last question — are there any known issues with large orgs in procurement? lead times?
[07:38] Austen: procurement tends to take a few weeks for enterprise; pilot can run under a pilot MSA much faster — most of the time we can get going once the security packet is accepted and a PO/credit agreement is signed.
[07:50] Priya: ok great. let's recap next steps.
[07:53] Austen: recap: Redwood sends pilot plan + security packet + pilot credit estimate (action: Austen), customer shares prompt set and infra contact (action: Priya/Carlos), schedule benchmark (target 9/16) (action: Maya/Jonah to coordinate).
[08:10] Priya: sounds good.
[08:12] Ella: i'll look out for the security docs.
[08:14] Maya: quick note — we might recommend starting on hosted with lower-latency model v1, then toggle to reserved pool if we see consistent p95 misses; we can automate fallback policies to quantized variant on load.
[08:29] Priya: i'm comfortable with that approach.
[08:31] Austen: awesome — we'll follow up with times for the benchmark and the pilot packet today. thanks everyone.

[08:36] End call.
